task: Forecasting and Anomaly Detection (Final Scientific Verification Pass)

india_dataset.exclusion_reason: Insufficient historical years (< 5 distinct years of data). This is an experimental eligibility rule, not a hydrological law.
india_dataset.anomaly_type: Descriptive Historical Anomaly Analysis (Not Causal Real-Time Alerts)

conclusions: India dataset (Full Eligible Population): Persistence provides a very strong baseline (R2: 0.84), significantly outperforming Seasonal Historical (R2: 0.13) and ML models (Linear: 0.07, HistGB: -0.16) for a one-step-ahead next-observation prediction.

Maharashtra dataset: 6-hourly telemetry has extremely high autocorrelation. Persistence baseline achieves near-perfect R2 (0.995). The ML model failed to capture dynamics significantly better than Persistence for predicting the next observation.
Absolute chronological splitting with zero temporal leakage was successfully enforced across the entire eligible scientific population.
The anomaly detector utilizes full dataset seasonal means and therefore represents descriptive historical anomaly analysis, not a production-ready real-time causal alerting system.
